lists.name: Unnamed List (Items 11-57)
lists.of: characteristics of a spatial network (likely caves)
items: 11. Course or outline is [undular, wiggly, squirmy, helical, or angular].
16. Develops and has types of speleothems [accretions, concretions, protrusions, barriers, crystals, drapes, e/vc].
20. Ellipsoidal or lenticular (as to overall 3-dimensional shape of network).
22. Exhibits growth [extension, cross-section enlargement, arborescence, e/vc].
24. Flow-bearing, translocates things or materials, and/or is path-like.
26. Formed by processes of [erosion, solution, corrosion, collapse, removal, e/vc].
27. Formed in [joints, faults, interstrata beds, weak layers, porous matter, e/vc].
29. Has one opening (single entrance sans back exit).
32. Hollow, evacuated, or negative (represents simple absence of matric substance).
37. Involves nothingness [is dark, silent, colorless, lifeless, e/vc].
38. Involves temporally [uniform, static, eventless, or stagnant] conditions [thermal, hygroscopic, biological, etc].
40. Liable to undergo accidental self-sealing or fragmentation.
47. Mysterious, or disorienting to human visitor.
50. Passes through multistage birth-to-death life cycle [born, grows, matures, ages, and dies].
52. Poly-cyclic; can become quiescent or fossil-like and then be reactivated.

notes: The list is a continuation from a previous page and appears to describe the properties of cave systems or similar geological networks. Typographical anomalies from the typewriter, such as an 'ö' appearing where a space was likely intended (e.g. items 19 and 57), have been transcribed verbatim.
